english: You were in Berlin last week. (du)
The children were in the garden.
Did you have a nice holiday? (Sie)
My grandfather had a big farm.
As a child I had a cat.
I had a lot to do.
Were you able to help him? (du)
I had to work on Saturday.
He had to go to the doctor.
We had to wait a long time.
You had to get up early. (ihr)
I wanted to become a doctor.
They wanted to buy a house.
What did you want to say? (du)
We were allowed to stay up late.
As a child I wasn't allowed to watch TV.
I was supposed to call him.
You were supposed to be here at eight. (du)
We were supposed to bring something.
She was supposed to stay in bed.
She lived in Munich for a long time.
The book lay on the table.
The glass fell on the floor.

note: The general rule (no ending in the ich and er/sie/es forms) doesn't apply here: werden is an exception, and ich/er/sie/es wurde ends in -e (du wurdest, wir wurden).

english: She took the children to school.
